title: Will the model fit (looks hard, is easy)
prompt_text: I want to run a 7-billion-parameter model in bfloat16 on a GPU with 12 GB of memory. Quantisation is not an option. The KV cache costs 0.5 MB per token per sequence at this model size, I want a 4,096-token context, and I was thinking of batch sizes of 1, 2 or 4. Activations are small enough to ignore. Which batch size should I use, and how much memory will be left over?

content:
**Short answer:**  
With a 12 GB GPU you can’t run a 7 B‑parameter model in bfloat16 and keep a 4 096‑token KV cache, no matter how small the batch size you try. Even for **batch = 1** you would need ≈ 16 GB of VRAM, leaving you ~ ‑4 GB (i.e. you’re over the limit). Below is a step‑by‑step breakdown of the memory requirements and what would be possible (or not) if you change any of the variables. ---

## 1. Memory budget for a 7 B bfloat16 model

| Component | Size (bytes) | Size (GB) |
|-----------|--------------|------------|
| **Model weights** (7 B × 2 bytes) | 7 × 10⁹ × 2 = 1.4 × 10¹⁰ B | **≈ 14 GB** |
| **KV cache** (0.5 MiB / token / seq) × 4 096 tokens | 0.5 MiB × 4096 ≈ 2 048 MiB | **≈ 2 GB** |
| **Activations** (assumed negligible) | – | ~0 GB |
| **Total (batch = 1)** | – | **≈ 16 GB** |

### What this means
- **Weights alone already consume ~14 GB**, which already exceeds a 12 GB GPU. - Adding the KV cache pushes the requirement to **≈ 16 GB** for a single token stream. - Activations are usually only a few hundred megabytes for a 7 B model, so they won’t rescue the situation. ---

## 2. How batch size multiplies the KV cache

The KV cache is *per sequence* and grows linearly with the batch size **B**. | Batch size **B** | KV cache (B × 2 GB) | Total VRAM needed (≈ 14 GB + KV) |
|-------------------|----------------------|-----------------------------------|
| 1 | 2 GB | **≈ 16 GB** |
| 2 | 4 GB | **≈ 18 GB** |
| 4 | 8 GB | **≈ 20 GB** |

All three numbers are **greater than 12 GB**, so **no batch size fits**. ---

## 3. What you can (or can’t) do with a 12 GB card

| Option | What it buys you | Why it’s insufficient (or viable) |
|--------|------------------|-----------------------------------|
| **Reduce the KV context** (e.g., 2 K tokens) | Cuts KV to ~1 GB, total ≈ 15 GB | Still >12 GB. |
| **Trim the model** (e.g., a 5 B or 3 B sub‑model) | Smaller weight footprint | You no longer have the 7 B model you wanted. |
| **Quantise weights** (8‑bit / 4‑bit) | 7 B × 1 byte ≈ 7 GB (8‑bit) or 3.5 GB (4‑bit) | You explicitly said quantisation isn’t an option. |
| **Off‑load parts of the model to CPU** (CPU‑RAM + GPU‑swap) | Keeps 7 B in RAM, streams layers to GPU | Inference speed drops dramatically, and you still need a GPU with enough memory to hold the active layers plus KV (≈ 9 GB for a single layer). |
| **Multi‑GPU pipeline / tensor parallelism** | Split weights across GPUs (e.g., 2 × 7 B/2 ≈ 3.5 B per GPU) | With two 12 GB GPUs you could host ~3.5 B × 2 ≈ 7 GB each, plus KV ≈ 2 GB → ~9 GB per GPU, which *fits* a single GPU in a 2‑GPU pipeline. This is the only realistic way to run the full 7 B model on 12 GB cards. |
| **Use a larger‑VRAM GPU** (≥ 16 GB, preferably ≥ 18 GB) | Directly fits the 7 B bfloat16 + KV budget | Simple but requires buying a GPU with ≥ 16 GB (e.g., RTX 4090, A100 40 GB, etc.). |

---

## 4. Bottom‑line recommendation

| Goal | Feasibility on a **single 12 GB GPU** |
|------|--------------------------------------|
| Run **full 7 B bfloat16** + **4 096‑token KV** with any batch size | **Impossible** (need ~16 GB minimum, ~18 GB for batch 2, ~20 GB for batch 4). |
| Run a **smaller model** (≤ 5 B) with 4 096 KV | **Possible** – e.g., a 4.7 B bfloat16 model ≈ 9.4 GB + 2 GB KV ≈ 11.4 GB (fits, leaving < 0.6 GB slack). |
| Keep the 7 B model but **share GPUs** | **Yes** – split weights across 2–4 GPUs using tensor/pipeline parallelism; each GPU holds ~3.5 B × 2 ≈ 7 GB + KV ≈ 2 GB → ~9 GB per GPU. |
| Off‑load **weights to CPU** and stream layers to GPU | **Works** but will be extremely slow; you’ll still need a GPU with enough free VRAM for the active layers + KV. |
| **Quantise** the model | **Would fit**, but you said quantisation isn’t an option. |

---

## 5. Quick “what‑if” numbers for a **batch = 1** 7 B run

| Memory component | Bytes |
|------------------|-------|
| Model weights (bfloat16) | 14 GB |
| KV cache (4096 tokens) | 2 GB |
| Activations (≈ 0.2 GB) | 0.2 GB |
| **Total** | **≈ 16.2 GB** |

*Result:* You need **≈ 16 GB** of VRAM, i.e. **~4 GB** more than a 12 GB GPU provides. **Therefore the answer to your original question is:**  
> *You cannot pick a batch size that fits. Even batch = 1 exceeds the GPU’s memory, so the model will not run on a 12 GB GPU without further tricks (multi‑GPU parallelism, weight off‑loading, or a smaller model). *

---

### TL;DR (one‑sentence)

- **No batch size (1, 2, 4) will fit a 7 B bfloat16 model with a 4 096‑token KV cache on a 12 GB GPU; you need roughly 16 GB just for one sequence, so you must either use a larger‑VRAM GPU, split the model across GPUs, or reduce the model size (or quantise, which you ruled out). **
